name: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām al-Harawī
summary: Scholar of language, hadith and law, author of Gharīb al-ḥadīth and al-Gharīb al-muṣannaf; judge of Tarsus, who died in Mecca.
bio: Abū ʿUbayd was born in Herat, the son of a Byzantine slave, and learnt the language from the Basrans and the Kufans alike, from al-Aṣmaʿī and Abū ʿUbayda as from al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ; al-Zubaydī places him in the third generation of the Kufan lexicographers. He served as judge of Tarsus on the Byzantine frontier for eighteen years.

His Gharīb al-ḥadīth explains the rare words of the hadith and was the model of later books of its kind; al-Gharīb al-muṣannaf arranges the rare words of Arabic by subject; his Kitāb al-Amwāl, on public finance in Islamic law, and his Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān are classics of their fields. He died in Mecca in 224/838.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 123 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
